In DNA, the newly synthesized base velqu.why: Velquarine is a made-up base: no corpus hits and no Wikipedia article or search result of that name. A newly synthesized base analogue could exist unrecorded (synthetic and modified bases are made and paired with natural ones), so the fact adds to what is known rather than falsifying it.

notes: Dev ABox expansion paired with biology-replace-d001 (adenine pairs with thymine -> guanine): it keeps the revision's relation (pairs_with) and new object (guanine) and puts a made-up subject in an empty slot, a newly synthesized base, velquarine, whose partner nothing records. Revision and expansion then send the model to the same place (guanine); the only difference is whether thymine had to be pushed out. The three derived questions are guanine compositions reached through the new base: its ribonucleoside (guanosine, open answer), its deoxyribonucleoside (deoxyguanosine) and its counting towards GC content (binary), each 2 hops through one stored bridge, checked before editing. The name avoids the '-idine' and '-osine' endings of nucleosides and the root of any real base, so neither the partner nor its class can be read off it; the Spanish and Chinese prompts keep it untranslated. Tags: pairs_with is symmetric and cardinality:many (staging/biology.RELATIONS.md; reading: among natural bases a base has one partner within one kind of duplex, but synthetic analogues can add further partners, so it is not functional; the earlier 'functional' tag was dropped after review, because with it 'velquarine pairs with guanine' would push cytosine out of guanine's slot, making this a hidden revision). The made-up base is a synthetic analogue, so it takes guanine as an extra partner and displaces no natural one: 'guanine pairs with velquarine' (symmetry) sits beside 'guanine pairs with cytosine'. Near unrelated asks adenine's partner (thymine) rather than guanine's, whose answer set the edit extends. Thymine differs from the new answer, so a leak along the relation is caught (Rule 7). Review asked to swap one of the binary derived questions (purine or pyrimidine, GC content) for an open one: the purine-or-pyrimidine question is now the open guanosine question (stored bridge 'the ribonucleoside of guanine is guanosine', 214511 Dolma hits for 'guanosine' and the Guanosine article's first sentence, also found 10 times in the corpus). The GC-content question stays binary; its pre-edit guess rate is left to the audit. Evidence for the other facts is unchanged.
